'''''Achyrocline satureioides''''', commonly known as '''macela''' or '''marcela''', is a species of plant in the family [[Asteraceae]]. It is native to [[South America]], from [[Argentina]] to [[Colombia]] to [[Guyana]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Achyrocline satureioides - Useful Tropical Plants|url=http://tropical.theferns.info/viewtropical.php?id=Achyrocline+satureioides|access-date=2021-03-25|website=tropical.theferns.info|archive-date=2021-04-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210414170235/http://tropical.theferns.info/viewtropical.php?id=Achyrocline+satureioides|url-status=live}}</ref> A semi-annual [[herbaceous plant]] reaching about a meter tall, it has simple, narrow green [[Leaf|leaves]] with serrated edges. It produces yellow [[flower]]s in [[raceme]]s around [[Easter]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Macela (Achyrocline Satureioides) 🏡 Gardening|url=https://en.eco-designfinca.com/macela-472|access-date=2021-03-25|website=Online Magazine|language=en-US|archive-date=2023-04-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407131921/https://en.eco-designfinca.com/macela-472|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Uses ==
It is used as the [[medicinal plant]] symbol of [[Rio Grande do Sul]] state in Brazil. This plant is widely used in various countries which share the Guarani cultural heritage such as Paraguay, Uruguay, and northern Argentina,<ref>{{cite journal|author=Dellacassa, Eduardo|title=Marcela, a promising medicinal and aromatic plant from Latin America: A review|journal=Industrial Crops and Products|publisher=[[Elsevier]]|volume=33|issue=1|year=2012|issn=0926-6690}}</ref> where it is used to treat stomach, digestive, and gastrointestinal disorders.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |date=August 29, 2017 |title=Supplementation with Achyrocline satureioides Inflorescence Extracts to Pregnant and Breastfeeding Rats Induces Tissue-Specific Changes in Enzymatic Activity and Lower Neonatal Survival |pmc=5618311 |last1=Moresco |first1=K. S. |last2=Silveira |first2=A. K. |last3=Schnorr |first3=C. E. |last4=Zeidán-Chuliá |first4=F. |last5=Bortolin |first5=R. C. |last6=Bittencourt |first6=L. D. |last7=Mingori |first7=M. |last8=Heimfarth |first8=L. |last9=Rabelo |first9=T. K. |last10=Morrone |first10=M. D. |last11=Carini |first11=J. P. |last12=Gelain |first12=D. P. |last13=Bassani |first13=V. L. |last14=Moreira |first14=J. C. |journal=Biomedicines |volume=5 |issue=3 |page=53 |doi=10.3390/biomedicines5030053 |pmid=29093434 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

The species' extract, which contains [[isorhamnetin]], [[luteolin]], and [[quercetin]], is used to fight [[herpes simplex|herpes]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Bidone J.|author2=Argenta D.F.|author3=Kratz J.|author4=Pettenuzzo L.F.|author5=Horn A.P.|author6=Koester L.S.|author7=Bassani V.L.|author8=Simões C.M.|author9=Teixeira H.F.|title=Antiherpes Activity and Skin/Mucosa Distribution of Flavonoids from Achyrocline satureioides Extract Incorporated into Topical Nanoemulsions.|journal=[[BioMed Research International]]|volume=2015|year=2015|doi=10.1155/2015/238010|pmid=26101767|pmc=4458523|pages=1–7|doi-access=free}}</ref> A. saturejoides extract might have antiviral effects against the [[Western equine encephalitis virus]]. The extract could also have [[immunomodulatory]] properties. In general, it can help with the management of viral respiratory infections, including [[SARS-CoV-2]] also known as Covid.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Siqueira |first1=Ionara |last2=Simoes |first2=Claidia |last3=Bassani |first3=Valquiria |date=August 5, 2020 |title=Achyrocline satureioides (Lam.) D.C. as a potential approach for management of viral respiratory infections |journal=Phytotherapy Research|volume=35 |issue=1 |pages=3–5 |doi=10.1002/ptr.6807 |pmid=32757241 |pmc=7436611 }}</ref>

A. satureioides could also have effects on rat pregnancy. The rats had reduced delivery index and neonatal survival after being supplemented with ''[[Achyrocline satureioides]].'' This also has an impact on variations in tissue-specific redox [[homeostasis]] and [[enzymatic activity]], especially in the liver and kidney.<ref name=":0" />

It is also used extensively in South Portugal, in bonfires during popular celebrations where people enjoyed the smell of burnt marcela and chorizos... when unavailable, people would simply open shellfish in the fire pit, eat them with a bit of lemon and make traditional constructions from the leftover shells, an art passed throughout multiple generations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cm-murtosa.pt/pages/573|title=Tradicionais Fogueiras e dos Santos Populares|access-date=2020-06-12|archive-date=2020-06-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200619134154/https://www.cm-murtosa.pt/pages/573|url-status=live}}</ref>

The plant, or sometimes just the flowers, are used to make tea. The heads of the flowers are used to make medicinal wines and bitters. The flowers are also crushed up and put in a pillow to help sleep.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Achyrocline satureioides - Useful Tropical Plants |url=https://tropical.theferns.info/viewtropical.php?id=Achyrocline+satureioides |access-date=2023-08-22 |website=tropical.theferns.info |archive-date=2021-06-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210613121037/https://tropical.theferns.info/viewtropical.php?id=Achyrocline+satureioides |url-status=live }}</ref>
